query: 2026 Florida Republican gubernatorial primary status: Byron Donalds candidacy, opponents, Trump endorsement, polling, competitors dropping out. Who is running against Donalds and what are the polls showing as of mid-2026?
answer:
Research complete. Key takeaways:

**The question's premise has been overtaken by events** — the Florida primary was held August 18, 2026, one day before this research date. Donalds won.

**The four things worth flagging most:**

1. **Donalds won but underperformed.** 47.8% — below a majority against a split field, with Trump's endorsement, $111M raised, and no serious debate exposure. CNN's benchmark comparison was Trump-backed Andy Biggs taking ~74% in Arizona. GOP operatives quoted on the record are calling it "an actual vulnerability."

2. **The polls got the winner right and second place badly wrong.** RealClearPolling's final average had Donalds at 48.7 (actual 47.8 — near-perfect) but Collins at 11.2 against an actual 25.2. The 26–51% undecided share that persisted all cycle broke almost entirely to Collins.

3. **Nobody dropped out mid-race.** The "competitors dropping out" framing belongs to the *pre-filing* period: Casey DeSantis (killed by the Hope Florida $10M Medicaid-settlement scandal), Matt Gaetz, and Francis Suarez all declined without entering. On the Democratic side, Jerry Demings withdrew in June 2026 after a cancer diagnosis, clearing Jolly's path.

4. **DeSantis endorsed no one — including his own Lieutenant Governor.** That's the through-line of the whole primary, and CNN cites it as a plausible contributor to Donalds' soft margin.

**Two live items** as of today: Donalds has not named a running mate, with a hard statutory deadline of 5:00 p.m. ET August 27 (failure forfeits ballot position); and the most recent public general-election poll (Hart Research, D-aligned, Aug 10–13) shows Jolly +1 — against neutral/academic polls showing Donalds +5 to +7 and Cook/Inside Elections both rating the race Solid Republican.

Two source errors I'd caution against propagating: NBC's election-night piece dates the Trump endorsement to "May" (it was February 20, 2025, pre-announcement — corroborated five ways), and Ballotpedia's general-election page lists Sean Lozano as Donalds' running mate (Lozano was Fishback's).

key_facts: Byron Donalds WON the Florida Republican gubernatorial primary on August 18, 2026. AP called the race at 8:00 p.m. ET, immediately after the last polls closed; CNN and NBC News projected the same. The question's framing ('as of mid-2026') is now superseded by the actual result.

Donalds finished with 47.8% (810,552 votes) — BELOW 50% against a fragmented field. National press and GOP operatives treated this as an underperformance for a candidate with Trump's endorsement and ~$110M raised. CNN compared it unfavorably to Trump-backed Andy Biggs winning Arizona's GOP gubernatorial primary with ~74%.
Runner-up was Lt. Gov. Jay Collins with 25.2% (426,696 votes) — a margin of 22.6 points / 383,856 votes.

Full GOP field was 11 candidates. Four substantive: Byron Donalds (47.8%), Jay Collins (25.2%), James Fishback (10.5%), Paul Renner (8.5%). Minor: Bobby Williams (4.1%), Rachel Rodriguez (1.6%), Jim Holcomb (0.8%), James W. Shaw (0.5%), Arthur McCaffrey (0.4%), Caneste Succe (0.4%), Daniel Nokovich (0.3%).

Trump endorsed Donalds on Truth Social on February 20, 2025 — BEFORE Donalds announced ('RUN, BYRON, RUN!'). Donalds formally announced February 25–26, 2025. A Trump adviser told NBC in May 2025 the endorsement was 'set' for Donalds 'and only Donalds' regardless of who else entered.

Gov. Ron DeSantis (term-limited) endorsed NO ONE in the primary — not even his own appointed Lieutenant Governor, Jay Collins. He repeatedly raised questions about Donalds' candidacy and called Renner's entry 'ill-advised' before saying in August 2026 that Renner would make a 'good governor.'

No major candidate dropped out mid-race. The consequential exits were pre-filing declines: Casey DeSantis (never entered; prospects collapsed over the Hope Florida Foundation scandal involving $10M tied to a Medicaid settlement), Matt Gaetz (flirted Jan–May 2025, became an OAN host), and Francis Suarez (conceded Trump's endorsement of Donalds 'makes it hard').

Polling was accurate on Donalds but badly wrong on second place. RealClearPolling's Aug 14 average had Donalds 48.7 (actual 47.8) but Collins at only 11.2 (actual 25.2) — a 14-point miss. Undecideds, persistently 26–51% all cycle, broke overwhelmingly to Collins.

Donalds raised a record $110–111 million (USA TODAY Network, Florida Trib), spending $50M+ by mid-August. Backers included Ken Griffin and Elon Musk. Fishback's concession line: 'Our opposition had over $100 million. We had 1% of that, and yet we secured ten times as many votes as the dollars we raised.'

The Republican Party of Florida set a debate qualification threshold only Donalds could clear and declined to hold a primary debate. Donalds skipped the June 27 'Sunshine State Showdown' forum and the July 2 Patrick Bet-David-hosted debate. DeSantis publicly attacked the RPOF decision.

Jay Collins sued to disqualify James Fishback over the Florida constitution's seven-year residency requirement (citing Fishback's 2020 D.C. voting record and 2021 D.C. home purchase). A Leon County circuit judge dismissed the suit for insufficient evidence.

Fishback ran explicitly racialized attacks on Donalds, who is Black — calling him a 'slave' to his donors, a 'DEI Republican,' and claiming he'd 'turn Florida into a Section 8 ghetto.' The Republican Party of Florida condemned his 'antisemitic and racist attacks' in June 2026. He was endorsed by Tucker Carlson, Nick Fuentes, Andrew Tate, and Kyle Rittenhouse.

Collins named FDEM Director Kevin Guthrie as running mate on August 17, 2026 — the evening before the primary, reportedly asked only hours beforehand and without notifying DeSantis, who had appointed Guthrie in 2021.

Donalds faces Democrat David Jolly on November 3, 2026. Jolly, a former Republican congressman (2014–2017) who registered Democrat in 2025, won his primary with 61.0% over Dayna Foster (15.1%) and Dotie Joseph (9.6%). Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings, his most serious potential rival, dropped out in June 2026 after a cancer diagnosis.

Donalds has NOT yet named a lieutenant governor running mate as of August 19, 2026. Under Fla. Stat. 99.063(1) and the 2026 State Qualifying Handbook, the deadline is 5:00 p.m. ET, August 27, 2026; failure forfeits general-election ballot position. Jolly named Gwen Graham unusually early, on June 10, 2026.
Race ratings: Cook Political Report and Inside Elections both Solid Republican; Sabato's Crystal Ball Likely Republican (downgraded from Safe Republican on July 28, 2026).

General election polling is far closer than the ratings suggest and splits by sponsor. The most recent public survey — Hart Research (D-aligned, DGA-released, Aug 10–13, 600 LV) — shows Jolly 46, Donalds 45, with Jolly leading independents 48–37 and Donalds' favorables underwater (40/43 overall, 34/48 among independents). Neutral/academic polls (UNF July: Donalds 46–41; Emerson March: 44–39; JMI July: 45–38) show Donalds +5 to +7.

Republican structural advantages: ~1.5 million more registered Republicans than Democrats; Trump won Florida by 13 points in 2024; DeSantis beat Charlie Crist 59.4–40.0 in 2022; no Democrat has won a Florida governorship since Lawton Chiles in 1994.
If Donalds wins in November he would be Florida's first African-American governor and the first Black Republican governor in U.S. history.

Data centers and AI were the primary's sleeper substantive issue. Donalds took money from AI interests and argued Florida should embrace Big Tech/data-center development while insulating ratepayers; Renner called for a 12–24 month moratorium and Fishback for a statewide ban.
